title: Lunit INSIGHT CXR flags a subpulmonic effusion in an 87-year-old; ultrasound confirms, patient refuses transfer
summary: At an emergency service in the Algarve, Lunit INSIGHT CXR flagged bilateral pleural effusion on a chest radiograph; ultrasound confirmed a right subpulmonic effusion, and the patient refused transfer.
account: On 29 September 2023, Tejani and colleagues at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center published a study that checked chest-radiograph readings against computed tomography. They found that Lunit INSIGHT CXR detected pleural effusion about as well as second-year residents, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.82 against 0.86. Miravent et al. (Cureus, 7 February 2026) report an 87-year-old man with three days of dyspnea. He attended a basic emergency service of the Algarve Local Health Unit. Lunit INSIGHT CXR (Lunit Inc., Seoul) flagged bilateral pleural effusion on his chest radiograph. Its confidence was higher on the left (97%) than on the right (77%), because the right-sided subpulmonic distribution mimicked hemidiaphragm elevation. The radiographer performed a screening thoracic ultrasound, which confirmed a right subpulmonic effusion. The authors say that this informed management and prevented misclassification as diaphragmatic elevation. He received nebulized bronchodilators. Despite advice and an indication for transfer to a referral hospital, he refused, signed a discharge against medical advice and left. The authors declare no financial support. The case report was accepted and published on 7 February 2026 and gives no date for the visit.

evidence.citation: Tejani A, Dowling T, Sanampudi S, Yazdani R, Canan A, Malja E, Xi Y, Abbara S, Peshock RM, Kay FU. Deep Learning for Detection of Pneumothorax and Pleural Effusion on Chest Radiographs: Validation Against Computed Tomography, Impact on Resident Reading Time, and Interreader Concordance. Journal of Thoracic Imaging, 29 September 2023 (PMID 37884394). The authors are radiologists at the University of Texas Southwestern Medical Center who name the tool as INSIGHT CXR (Lunit) and declare that they have no conflict of interest. Against CT, the AI detected pleural effusion with an AUROC of 0.82, and second-year residents reached 0.86, so the study sets the general accuracy of the flag used in this case.
